concepts.def: The basic types a language provides: integer for whole numbers, real for decimals, Boolean for true/false, character and string for text.
A fixed-size collection of elements of the same type stored contiguously and accessed by numeric index, starting at zero in most languages.
A composite data structure grouping related fields, possibly of different types, under one identifier, such as a student's name, age and grade.
Two linear structures: a stack is last-in-first-out with push and pop, while a queue is first-in-first-out with enqueue and dequeue.
A chain of nodes each containing data and a pointer to the next node, making insertion and deletion cheap but random access slow.
A structure mapping keys to storage locations via a hash function, giving near-constant average time for lookup, insertion and deletion.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Types & Structures — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Types & Structures brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Types & Structures.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which data type is most appropriate for storing a value that is either True or False?
options: Integer
String
Boolean
Real

mcqs.q: An element of a two-dimensional array is identified by:
options: A single index
Two indices, typically row and column
Its value alone
A hash of its contents

mcqs.q: Which structure removes items in first-in-first-out order?
options: Stack
Binary tree
Queue
Hash table

mcqs.q: A record differs from an array because a record:
options: Can group fields of different data types under one identifier
Must contain elements all of the same type
Can only store numbers
Is always sorted automatically

mcqs.q: In a zero-indexed array of 10 elements, what is the index of the last element?
options: 9 - indices run from 0 to 9, so the last index is the length minus one.
1 - arrays end at index one.
Whichever item is the largest value.
10 - the last element's index equals the array's length.

mcqs.q: What data type is the value 7.0?
options: String - anything containing a dot is text.
Real (float) - the decimal point makes it a real number in most languages, even though its fractional part happens to be zero.
Integer - 7.0 is a whole number so it must be an integer.
1 - arrays end at index one.

mcqs.q: Which item does a stack remove first?
options: The first item that was added, because items leave in arrival order.
The most recently added item - stacks are LIFO, with both push and pop operating at the top.
Whichever item is the largest value.
String - anything containing a dot is text.
